enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
1057 PM MDT Wed Oct 14 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION...


.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 1013 PM MDT Wed Oct 14 2026

 - A strong backdoor cold front is set to arrive Thursday night,
   bringing gusty winds and well below normal temperatures into 
   the weekend. 

 - High Wind Warning is in effect for far west Texas and portions
   of southern New Mexico for Thursday night into Friday. Wind 
   gusts up to 60 mph are possible along mountain west slopes. 

 - Scattered rain showers starting Monday and continuing through
   next Thursday. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1013 PM MDT Wed Oct 14 2026

Very strong winds and much cooler temperatures are coming to 
Southern New Mexico and Far West Texas Thursday night and Friday.
A low pressure circulation in Colorado will exit the Rockies to 
the east Thursday morning. A significant push of cooler air from 
Canada will fill in behind the system and move further south. A 
very strong 1041 mb surface high is driving this air mass 
southward along the Front Range into New Mexico. 

The cold front boundary will reach the local area by late 
Thursday afternoon, reaching the El Paso and Las Cruces metro 
areas Thursday evening. There is tight pressure gradient packing 
and a low level jet with this front that will result in strong 
northeasterly to easterly winds spreading across the area 
Thursday evening through Friday afternoon. Sustained wind speeds 
of 30 to 40 mph with wind gusts exceeding 60 mph are expected 
begin Thursday evening and lasting into Friday for Otero, El Paso,
and Hudspeth Counties. A High wind warning has been issued for the
previously mentioned counties along with Hidalgo and southern 
Grant counties where wind speeds will reach warning criteria on 
Friday. 

The remainder of the forecast area will experience strong 
winds reaching wind advisory levels with  gusts to 50 mph, but 
are expected to remain below wind warning levels. Blowing dust is 
likely with the strong winds, especially in El Paso and Hudspeth 
counties along with southern portions of Dona Ana, Luna counties 
beginning late Thursday evening. Blowing dust is also expected 
along the playas in Hidalgo county on Friday. 

Much cooler temperatures are also expected Friday into Saturday 
with day time high temperatures struggling to reach the lower 60s 
in the lowlands. Many areas will see temperatures as much as 12 to
16 degrees below normal Friday and Saturday. Freezing 
temperatures are expected for the mountains Friday and Saturday 
mornings. 

Chances for precipitation through Saturday remain near zero. A
potential moisture surge into the area, hinted at by previous 
model forecasts, has shifted south and is not expected to be a 
factor in our local weather pattern through the weekend. 

The long term outlook for Sunday and much of next week looks
wetter and warmer. A weakening low pressure system off of the Baja
Peninsula will move into the desert southwest, pulling subtropical
moisture into the region as early as Sunday afternoon. There will
be a slight chance of showers for the bootheel on Sunday afternoon
with a greater chance of showers across the region starting Monday
afternoon through next Thursday. The main driver for the precip
will be a deep low pressure system dropping down along the west
coast before moving inland and through the region on Thursday.
There will be a chance of rain Monday afternoon through next
Thursday. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(06Z TAFS)
Issued at 1013 PM MDT Wed Oct 14 2026

VFR conditions expected through Thursday afternoon. Aside from 
morning FEW060-080, ceilings will be unlimited at all four TAF 
sites. Some low end gusty winds from the west will be present for 
a few hours in the afternoon before dropping off and shifting more
northerly in the late afternoon. 

After 00Z a strong cold front will arrive from the northeast 
tomorrow evening. Winds will shift to the northeast and become 
very strong. Winds will be at least 08030G40KT with higher gusts 
to 50 knots possible. Some blowing dust is likely at KELP
beginning 03Z Thursday night through 18Z Friday. Low level wind 
shear will also occur after 00Z Thursday night, especially over 
KELP.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 931 AM MDT Wed Oct 14 2026

Limited fire weather concerns today and tomorrow. Min RHs today
will be above 20%, and for Thursday, lowland Min RHs will be in
the mid-to-upper teens and up to 30% in the mountains. Low end
gusty winds from the west likely by this afternoon and the north
on Thursday.

A strong backdoor cold front (moving east to west) will move into
the region Thursday night. Winds will shift to the east in the
evening hours and increase drastically. The strongest winds will
be west of the area mountains as well as Otero, Hudspeth, and El
Paso Counties. Sustained wind speeds of 25-35 mph likely for most
of the region, with high-end wind gusts reaching 60 mph in the
mountains. The strong winds will continue into Friday before
diminishing slightly on Saturday. Precipitation chances will be
low on Friday and Saturday, favoring out east in West Texas as
well as the area mountains. The high mountains may even see a
wintry mix early Saturday morning.
